dialogue.text: Hi everyone! In this video, I will introduce the past simple English tense.
dialogue.zh: 大家好！在這個影片中，我將介紹英文的過去簡單式。
dialogue.ja: みなさん、こんにちは！この動画では、英語の過去形（過去簡単時制）を紹介します。
dialogue.local: Hi everyone! In this video, I will introduce the past simple English tense.
dialogue.en: Hi everyone! In this video, I will introduce the past simple English tense.

dialogue.text: This grammar tense can help you explain a past general state, action, or habit. There's a lot to learn and it's a very important tense, so keep watching.
dialogue.zh: 這個文法時態可以幫助你說明過去的一般狀態、動作或習慣。內容很多且非常重要，請繼續觀看。
dialogue.ja: この文法時制は、過去の一般的な状態、行動、または習慣を説明するのに役立ちます。学ぶことがたくさんあり、とても重要な時制なので、ぜひ見続けてください。
dialogue.local: This grammar tense can help you explain a past general state, action, or habit. There's a lot to learn and it's a very important tense, so keep watching.
dialogue.en: This grammar tense can help you explain a past general state, action, or habit. There's a lot to learn and it's a very important tense, so keep watching.

dialogue.text: In this video, I will talk about the B verb in the past simple tense. The B verb in the past simple tense can be used to describe a past general state. We use the B verbs was and were in this tense. Take a look at the examples.
dialogue.zh: 在這個影片中，我會談論過去簡單式的B動詞。過去簡單式的B動詞可以用來描述過去的一般狀態。我們在這個時態中使用was和were這兩個B動詞。請看以下例子。
dialogue.ja: この動画では、過去形のB動詞について話します。過去形のB動詞は過去の一般的な状態を表すのに使われます。この時制ではwasとwereを使います。例を見てみましょう。
dialogue.local: In this video, I will talk about the B verb in the past simple tense. The B verb in the past simple tense can be used to describe a past general state. We use the B verbs was and were in this tense. Take a look at the examples.
dialogue.en: In this video, I will talk about the B verb in the past simple tense. The B verb in the past simple tense can be used to describe a past general state. We use the B verbs was and were in this tense. Take a look at the examples.

dialogue.text: I was scared. James or he was a teacher. She was sad. My dog was hungry. My dog can be it. So for I, he, she, it, we use the past tense B verb was.
dialogue.zh: 我感到害怕。James或他是老師。她很難過。我的狗很餓。我的狗可以用it代替。所以對於I、he、she、it，我們使用過去式的B動詞was。
dialogue.ja: 私は怖かった。ジェームズや彼は先生でした。彼女は悲しかった。私の犬はお腹が空いていました。犬はitで表せます。だから、I、he、she、itの場合は過去形のB動詞wasを使います。
dialogue.local: I was scared. James or he was a teacher. She was sad. My dog was hungry. My dog can be it. So for I, he, she, it, we use the past tense B verb was.
dialogue.en: I was scared. James or he was a teacher. She was sad. My dog was hungry. My dog can be it. So for I, he, she, it, we use the past tense B verb was.

dialogue.text: However, for you, we, and they, we use were. You were a good student. Your parents, or they, were at the park. And we were at home for two hours.
dialogue.zh: 然而，對於you、we和they，我們使用were。你是個好學生。你的父母，或者他們，在公園。我們在家待了兩個小時。
dialogue.ja: しかし、you、we、theyの場合はwereを使います。あなたは良い学生でした。あなたの両親、または彼らは公園にいました。そして私たちは2時間家にいました。
dialogue.local: However, for you, we, and they, we use were. You were a good student. Your parents, or they, were at the park. And we were at home for two hours.
dialogue.en: However, for you, we, and they, we use were. You were a good student. Your parents, or they, were at the park. And we were at home for two hours.

dialogue.text: In this last sentence, you see that the duration is emphasized. Great job. Let's move on.
dialogue.zh: 在最後這句話中，你會看到強調了持續時間。做得很好，我們繼續。
dialogue.ja: 最後の文では、期間が強調されています。よくできました。次に進みましょう。
dialogue.local: In this last sentence, you see that the duration is emphasized. Great job. Let's move on.
dialogue.en: In this last sentence, you see that the duration is emphasized. Great job. Let's move on.

dialogue.text: Now, I will talk about regular verbs in the past simple tense. Take a look at these examples.
dialogue.zh: 現在，我將談論過去簡單式的規則動詞。請看這些例子。
dialogue.ja: 次に、過去形の規則動詞について話します。これらの例を見てください。
dialogue.local: Now, I will talk about regular verbs in the past simple tense. Take a look at these examples.
dialogue.en: Now, I will talk about regular verbs in the past simple tense. Take a look at these examples.

dialogue.text: Liam played a game. Liam is a he, but really it doesn't matter for regular verbs in the past simple tense. Because no matter what the subject is, all we have to do is add D or ED to the end of the verb.
dialogue.zh: Liam玩了一場遊戲。Liam是男性，但對於過去簡單式的規則動詞來說，主詞是誰並不重要。因為不管主詞是什麼，我們只要在動詞後面加上D或ED。
dialogue.ja: リアムはゲームをしました。リアムは男性ですが、過去形の規則動詞では主語は関係ありません。どんな主語でも動詞の後ろにDかEDを付けるだけです。
dialogue.local: Liam played a game. Liam is a he, but really it doesn't matter for regular verbs in the past simple tense. Because no matter what the subject is, all we have to do is add D or ED to the end of the verb.
dialogue.en: Liam played a game. Liam is a he, but really it doesn't matter for regular verbs in the past simple tense. Because no matter what the subject is, all we have to do is add D or ED to the end of the verb.

dialogue.text: Here, the verb is play. So I added ED. Liam played a game.
dialogue.zh: 這裡的動詞是play，所以我加上了ED。Liam played a game。
dialogue.ja: ここでは動詞はplayです。だからEDを付けました。リアムはゲームをしました。
dialogue.local: Here, the verb is play. So I added ED. Liam played a game.
dialogue.en: Here, the verb is play. So I added ED. Liam played a game.

dialogue.text: The car or it needed gas. The verb here is need for the past simple tense I added ED.
dialogue.zh: 車子或它需要加油。這裡的動詞是need，過去簡單式我加上了ED。
dialogue.ja: 車やそれはガソリンが必要でした。ここでの動詞はneedで、過去形にするためにEDを付けました。
dialogue.local: The car or it needed gas. The verb here is need for the past simple tense I added ED.
dialogue.en: The car or it needed gas. The verb here is need for the past simple tense I added ED.

dialogue.text: We watched a movie. Again, an ED at the end of watch.
dialogue.zh: 我們看了一部電影。watch後面又加了ED。
dialogue.ja: 私たちは映画を見ました。watchの後ろにEDを付けました。
dialogue.local: We watched a movie. Again, an ED at the end of watch.
dialogue.en: We watched a movie. Again, an ED at the end of watch.

dialogue.text: You exercised for an hour. In this case, the verb is exercise. I only need to add a D to make it the past tense.
dialogue.zh: 你運動了一個小時。這裡的動詞是exercise，我只需要加D來變成過去式。
dialogue.ja: あなたは1時間運動しました。この場合、動詞はexerciseで、過去形にするためにDだけを付けます。
dialogue.local: You exercised for an hour. In this case, the verb is exercise. I only need to add a D to make it the past tense.
dialogue.en: You exercised for an hour. In this case, the verb is exercise. I only need to add a D to make it the past tense.

dialogue.text: And finally, they usually worked after school. The verb is work and I added an ED to make it in the past tense. The word usually shows that this was a habit.
dialogue.zh: 最後，他們通常放學後工作。動詞是work，我加了ED變成過去式。usually這個字表示這是一個習慣。
dialogue.ja: 最後に、彼らは普段放課後に働いていました。動詞はworkで、過去形にするためにEDを付けました。usuallyは習慣を表します。
dialogue.local: And finally, they usually worked after school. The verb is work and I added an ED to make it in the past tense. The word usually shows that this was a habit.
dialogue.en: And finally, they usually worked after school. The verb is work and I added an ED to make it in the past tense. The word usually shows that this was a habit.

dialogue.text: Remember, the past simple tense can be used to show past habits. Let's move on.
dialogue.zh: 記住，過去簡單式可以用來表示過去的習慣。我們繼續。
dialogue.ja: 過去形は過去の習慣を表すことができます。続けましょう。
dialogue.local: Remember, the past simple tense can be used to show past habits. Let's move on.
dialogue.en: Remember, the past simple tense can be used to show past habits. Let's move on.

dialogue.text: Now, I'll talk about irregular verbs in the past simple tense. Remember, for regular verbs, we only add D or ED to make a verb into the past tense. However, for irregular verbs, we have to change the verb in a different way.
dialogue.zh: 現在，我要談談過去簡單式的不規則動詞。記住，規則動詞只要加D或ED就能變成過去式，但不規則動詞則必須用不同的方式改變動詞。
dialogue.ja: 次に、過去形の不規則動詞について話します。規則動詞はDかEDを付けるだけですが、不規則動詞は別の方法で変化させます。
dialogue.local: Now, I'll talk about irregular verbs in the past simple tense. Remember, for regular verbs, we only add D or ED to make a verb into the past tense. However, for irregular verbs, we have to change the verb in a different way.
dialogue.en: Now, I'll talk about irregular verbs in the past simple tense. Remember, for regular verbs, we only add D or ED to make a verb into the past tense. However, for irregular verbs, we have to change the verb in a different way.

dialogue.text: Let's take a look at some examples. I ate with my friend. The verb here is eat. Eat is the past simple tense of eat.
dialogue.zh: 讓我們看一些例子。我和朋友吃飯。這裡的動詞是eat，ate是eat的過去簡單式。
dialogue.ja: いくつか例を見てみましょう。私は友達と食事をしました。動詞はeatで、ateはeatの過去形です。
dialogue.local: Let's take a look at some examples. I ate with my friend. The verb here is eat. Eat is the past simple tense of eat.
dialogue.en: Let's take a look at some examples. I ate with my friend. The verb here is eat. Eat is the past simple tense of eat.

dialogue.text: The next example says Nara wrote a story. The verb is write and because it's irregular to change it into the past tense, we change the verb to wrote.
dialogue.zh: 下一個例子是Nara寫了一個故事。動詞是write，因為是不規則動詞，所以改成wrote。
dialogue.ja: 次の例は、ナラが物語を書きました。動詞はwriteで、不規則動詞なので過去形はwroteになります。
dialogue.local: The next example says Nara wrote a story. The verb is write and because it's irregular to change it into the past tense, we change the verb to wrote.
dialogue.en: The next example says Nara wrote a story. The verb is write and because it's irregular to change it into the past tense, we change the verb to wrote.

dialogue.text: You often came home late. The verb here is come and it's been changed to came. You'll notice that we had the word often to show a habit.
dialogue.zh: 你經常回家很晚。這裡的動詞是come，改成了came。你會注意到often這個字表示習慣。
dialogue.ja: あなたはよく遅く帰宅しました。動詞はcomeで、過去形はcameです。oftenは習慣を示しています。
dialogue.local: You often came home late. The verb here is come and it's been changed to came. You'll notice that we had the word often to show a habit.
dialogue.en: You often came home late. The verb here is come and it's been changed to came. You'll notice that we had the word often to show a habit.

dialogue.text: We bought a camera. The verb here is buy and it's been changed to bought to show the past simple tense.
dialogue.zh: 我們買了一台相機。這裡的動詞是buy，改成了bought表示過去簡單式。
dialogue.ja: 私たちはカメラを買いました。動詞はbuyで、過去形はboughtです。
dialogue.local: We bought a camera. The verb here is buy and it's been changed to bought to show the past simple tense.
dialogue.en: We bought a camera. The verb here is buy and it's been changed to bought to show the past simple tense.

dialogue.text: And finally, my parents sent me money for a year. Here, the verb sent is the past tense of send. Here, we also see for a year. This shows duration.
dialogue.zh: 最後，我的父母給我錢持續了一年。這裡的動詞sent是send的過去式。for a year表示持續時間。
dialogue.ja: 最後に、私の両親は1年間お金を送ってくれました。動詞sentはsendの過去形です。for a yearは期間を示しています。
dialogue.local: And finally, my parents sent me money for a year. Here, the verb sent is the past tense of send. Here, we also see for a year. This shows duration.
dialogue.en: And finally, my parents sent me money for a year. Here, the verb sent is the past tense of send. Here, we also see for a year. This shows duration.

dialogue.text: Let's move on. Now, I will talk about the negative form for the B verb in the past simple tense. Here are some examples.
dialogue.zh: 我們繼續。現在，我要談談過去簡單式B動詞的否定形式。以下是一些例子。
dialogue.ja: 続けましょう。次に、過去形のB動詞の否定形について話します。いくつか例を見てみましょう。
dialogue.local: Let's move on. Now, I will talk about the negative form for the B verb in the past simple tense. Here are some examples.
dialogue.en: Let's move on. Now, I will talk about the negative form for the B verb in the past simple tense. Here are some examples.

dialogue.text: The first one says I was not hungry. For the past simple tense, the negative B verb, if the subject is I, he, she or it, we say was not. For example, I was not. Or she was not. Or the contraction wasn't. I wasn't. She wasn't.
dialogue.zh: 第一句是我不餓。過去簡單式的B動詞否定，如果主詞是I、he、she或it，我們說was not。例如：I was not，或she was not，縮寫是wasn't，如I wasn't，She wasn't。
dialogue.ja: 最初の例は「私はお腹が空いていませんでした」です。過去形のB動詞の否定形は、主語がI、he、she、itの場合、was notを使います。例えば、I was not、She was not、または短縮形のwasn't（I wasn't、She wasn't）です。
dialogue.local: The first one says I was not hungry. For the past simple tense, the negative B verb, if the subject is I, he, she or it, we say was not. For example, I was not. Or she was not. Or the contraction wasn't. I wasn't. She wasn't.
dialogue.en: The first one says I was not hungry. For the past simple tense, the negative B verb, if the subject is I, he, she or it, we say was not. For example, I was not. Or she was not. Or the contraction wasn't. I wasn't. She wasn't.

dialogue.text: So let's look again. I was not hungry. She wasn't home today.
dialogue.zh: 再看一次：我不餓。她今天不在家。
dialogue.ja: もう一度見てみましょう。I was not hungry. She wasn't home today.
dialogue.local: So let's look again. I was not hungry. She wasn't home today.
dialogue.en: So let's look again. I was not hungry. She wasn't home today.

dialogue.text: Now, if the subject is you, we or they, we say were not. Or the contraction weren't. The children or they were not quiet. The children were not quiet.
dialogue.zh: 現在，如果主詞是you、we或they，我們說were not，縮寫是weren't。孩子們或他們不安靜。孩子們不安靜。
dialogue.ja: 主語がyou、we、theyの場合はwere notを使い、短縮形はweren'tです。子供たちや彼らは静かではありませんでした。子供たちは静かではありませんでした。
dialogue.local: Now, if the subject is you, we or they, we say were not. Or the contraction weren't. The children or they were not quiet. The children were not quiet.
dialogue.en: Now, if the subject is you, we or they, we say were not. Or the contraction weren't. The children or they were not quiet. The children were not quiet.

dialogue.text: And then, the dog or it was not or wasn't playful.
dialogue.zh: 然後，狗或它不愛玩耍，可以說was not或wasn't。
dialogue.ja: そして、犬やそれは遊び好きではありませんでした。was notまたはwasn'tを使います。
dialogue.local: And then, the dog or it was not or wasn't playful.
dialogue.en: And then, the dog or it was not or wasn't playful.

dialogue.text: Let's move on. Now, let's talk about how to form the negative in the past simple tense for non B verbs, regular or irregular. Here are some examples.
dialogue.zh: 我們繼續。現在，談談非B動詞（規則或不規則）在過去簡單式的否定形式。以下是一些例子。
dialogue.ja: 続けましょう。次に、B動詞以外の規則・不規則動詞の過去形の否定形の作り方を説明します。例を見てみましょう。
dialogue.local: Let's move on. Now, let's talk about how to form the negative in the past simple tense for non B verbs, regular or irregular. Here are some examples.
dialogue.en: Let's move on. Now, let's talk about how to form the negative in the past simple tense for non B verbs, regular or irregular. Here are some examples.

dialogue.text: I did not like him. What we do for non B verbs is simply put did not after the subject. And you'll notice that for the verb, we don't make any changes. We keep the base verb.
dialogue.zh: 我不喜歡他。非B動詞的否定，只要在主詞後面加did not。動詞本身不變，保持原形。
dialogue.ja: I did not like him. B動詞以外の動詞の否定形は、主語の後にdid notを置きます。動詞は変えずに原形のままです。
dialogue.local: I did not like him. What we do for non B verbs is simply put did not after the subject. And you'll notice that for the verb, we don't make any changes. We keep the base verb.
dialogue.en: I did not like him. What we do for non B verbs is simply put did not after the subject. And you'll notice that for the verb, we don't make any changes. We keep the base verb.

dialogue.text: He didn't catch the ball. Again, it's he did not, but here we used a contraction. He didn't catch the ball.
dialogue.zh: 他沒有接到球。這是he did not的縮寫。He didn't catch the ball。
dialogue.ja: 彼はボールを捕まえませんでした。he did notの短縮形です。He didn't catch the ball。
dialogue.local: He didn't catch the ball. Again, it's he did not, but here we used a contraction. He didn't catch the ball.
dialogue.en: He didn't catch the ball. Again, it's he did not, but here we used a contraction. He didn't catch the ball.

dialogue.text: They didn't dance. Again, here's the contraction for did not. And you'll notice that for the verb, we didn't change it at all.
dialogue.zh: 他們沒有跳舞。這是did not的縮寫。動詞本身完全沒有改變。
dialogue.ja: 彼らは踊りませんでした。did notの短縮形です。動詞は全く変わっていません。
dialogue.local: They didn't dance. Again, here's the contraction for did not. And you'll notice that for the verb, we didn't change it at all.
dialogue.en: They didn't dance. Again, here's the contraction for did not. And you'll notice that for the verb, we didn't change it at all.

dialogue.text: Here's an irregular verb and here's a regular verb. We keep them in the base form. And finally, we didn't think about that. Again, we simply say did not or didn't.
dialogue.zh: 這裡有不規則動詞和規則動詞，我們都保持原形。最後，我們說we didn't think about that，簡單用did not或didn't。
dialogue.ja: これは不規則動詞で、こちらは規則動詞です。どちらも原形のままです。最後に、we didn't think about thatと言います。did notまたはdidn'tを使います。
dialogue.local: Here's an irregular verb and here's a regular verb. We keep them in the base form. And finally, we didn't think about that. Again, we simply say did not or didn't.
dialogue.en: Here's an irregular verb and here's a regular verb. We keep them in the base form. And finally, we didn't think about that. Again, we simply say did not or didn't.

dialogue.text: Let's move on. Now, I will introduce two ways to form questions for the past simple tense. Take a look at the first example. He was angry.
dialogue.zh: 我們繼續。現在，我將介紹兩種形成過去簡單式疑問句的方法。看第一個例子：He was angry。
dialogue.ja: 続けましょう。次に、過去形の疑問文の作り方を2つ紹介します。最初の例を見てください。He was angry.
dialogue.local: Let's move on. Now, I will introduce two ways to form questions for the past simple tense. Take a look at the first example. He was angry.
dialogue.en: Let's move on. Now, I will introduce two ways to form questions for the past simple tense. Take a look at the first example. He was angry.

dialogue.text: In this first sentence, we see the B verb was. It's quite easy. All you have to do to turn this into a question is switch the order of the first two words. Was he angry?
dialogue.zh: 在這句話中，我們看到B動詞was。很簡單，只要把前兩個字調換順序就變成疑問句：Was he angry?
dialogue.ja: この文ではB動詞wasがあります。簡単で、最初の2語の順番を入れ替えるだけで疑問文になります。Was he angry?
dialogue.local: In this first sentence, we see the B verb was. It's quite easy. All you have to do to turn this into a question is switch the order of the first two words. Was he angry?
dialogue.en: In this first sentence, we see the B verb was. It's quite easy. All you have to do to turn this into a question is switch the order of the first two words. Was he angry?

dialogue.text: You can answer by saying yes, he was or no, he wasn't.
dialogue.zh: 你可以回答是的，他是，或不是，他不是。
dialogue.ja: 答えは、Yes, he was または No, he wasn't です。
dialogue.local: You can answer by saying yes, he was or no, he wasn't.
dialogue.en: You can answer by saying yes, he was or no, he wasn't.

dialogue.text: The next sentence also has a B verb. They were comfortable. So again, switch the first two words. Were they comfortable?
dialogue.zh: 下一句也有B動詞。他們感到舒服。再把前兩個字調換：Were they comfortable?
dialogue.ja: 次の文もB動詞があります。They were comfortable。最初の2語を入れ替えます。Were they comfortable?
dialogue.local: The next sentence also has a B verb. They were comfortable. So again, switch the first two words. Were they comfortable?
dialogue.en: The next sentence also has a B verb. They were comfortable. So again, switch the first two words. Were they comfortable?

dialogue.text: The answers can be yes, they were or no, they weren't.
dialogue.zh: 回答可以是是的，他們是，或不是，他們不是。
dialogue.ja: 答えは Yes, they were または No, they weren't です。
dialogue.local: The answers can be yes, they were or no, they weren't.
dialogue.en: The answers can be yes, they were or no, they weren't.

dialogue.text: However, look at the third sentence. Sam lived here. There is no B verb in this sentence. Instead, we see the action verb lived.
dialogue.zh: 但是，看第三句。Sam住在這裡。這句沒有B動詞，而是動作動詞lived。
dialogue.ja: しかし、3番目の文を見てみましょう。Sam lived here。この文にはB動詞がなく、動作動詞のlivedがあります。
dialogue.local: However, look at the third sentence. Sam lived here. There is no B verb in this sentence. Instead, we see the action verb lived.
dialogue.en: However, look at the third sentence. Sam lived here. There is no B verb in this sentence. Instead, we see the action verb lived.

dialogue.text: So what we do is no matter what the subject, we start the question with did. Did Sam live here?
dialogue.zh: 所以不管主詞是誰，我們用did開頭問句：Did Sam live here?
dialogue.ja: だから、主語に関係なく、疑問文はdidで始めます。Did Sam live here?
dialogue.local: So what we do is no matter what the subject, we start the question with did. Did Sam live here?
dialogue.en: So what we do is no matter what the subject, we start the question with did. Did Sam live here?

dialogue.text: You'll notice that the verb no longer is in the past tense. We use the base form of the verb. Did Sam live here?
dialogue.zh: 你會注意到動詞不再是過去式，而是用原形。Did Sam live here?
dialogue.ja: 動詞は過去形ではなく原形を使います。Did Sam live here?
dialogue.local: You'll notice that the verb no longer is in the past tense. We use the base form of the verb. Did Sam live here?
dialogue.en: You'll notice that the verb no longer is in the past tense. We use the base form of the verb. Did Sam live here?

dialogue.text: You can say yes, he did or no, he didn't.
dialogue.zh: 你可以回答是的，他有，或不是，他沒有。
dialogue.ja: 答えは Yes, he did または No, he didn't です。
dialogue.local: You can say yes, he did or no, he didn't.
dialogue.en: You can say yes, he did or no, he didn't.

dialogue.text: The last sentence is similar. They won the contest last year. The verb here is won. That's not a B verb.
dialogue.zh: 最後一句類似。他們去年贏得比賽。動詞是won，這不是B動詞。
dialogue.ja: 最後の文も似ています。They won the contest last year。動詞はwonで、B動詞ではありません。
dialogue.local: The last sentence is similar. They won the contest last year. The verb here is won. That's not a B verb.
dialogue.en: The last sentence is similar. They won the contest last year. The verb here is won. That's not a B verb.

dialogue.text: So again, we start the question with did and then the subject they. We use the base form of the verb and that's win.
dialogue.zh: 所以我們用did開頭，接主詞they，動詞用原形win。
dialogue.ja: だから、疑問文はdidで始め、主語のtheyの後に動詞の原形winを使います。
dialogue.local: So again, we start the question with did and then the subject they. We use the base form of the verb and that's win.
dialogue.en: So again, we start the question with did and then the subject they. We use the base form of the verb and that's win.

dialogue.text: Did they win the contest last year? You can say yes, they did or no, they didn't.
dialogue.zh: Did they win the contest last year? 你可以回答是的，他們贏了，或不是，他們沒贏。
dialogue.ja: Did they win the contest last year? 答えは Yes, they did または No, they didn't です。
dialogue.local: Did they win the contest last year? You can say yes, they did or no, they didn't.
dialogue.en: Did they win the contest last year? You can say yes, they did or no, they didn't.

dialogue.text: Let's move on. Now I'll introduce how to create and answer WH questions in the past simple tense. Take a look at the board.
dialogue.zh: 我們繼續。現在我將介紹如何造和回答過去簡單式的WH疑問句。請看黑板。
dialogue.ja: 続けましょう。過去形のWH疑問文の作り方と答え方を紹介します。黒板を見てください。
dialogue.local: Let's move on. Now I'll introduce how to create and answer WH questions in the past simple tense. Take a look at the board.
dialogue.en: Let's move on. Now I'll introduce how to create and answer WH questions in the past simple tense. Take a look at the board.

dialogue.text: We have some WH words here. What? When? Where and why? You'll notice that after each WH word comes the word did.
dialogue.zh: 這裡有一些WH疑問詞：What、When、Where和Why。你會注意到每個WH字後面都接did。
dialogue.ja: ここにWH疑問詞があります。What、When、Where、Whyです。各WH疑問詞の後にdidが続きます。
dialogue.local: We have some WH words here. What? When? Where and why? You'll notice that after each WH word comes the word did.
dialogue.en: We have some WH words here. What? When? Where and why? You'll notice that after each WH word comes the word did.

dialogue.text: What did? When did? Where did and why did? What comes after that? The subject and then the base form of the verb.
dialogue.zh: What did？When did？Where did？Why did？接著是主詞，然後是動詞原形。
dialogue.ja: What did? When did? Where did? Why did? その後に主語が来て、動詞の原形が続きます。
dialogue.local: What did? When did? Where did and why did? What comes after that? The subject and then the base form of the verb.
dialogue.en: What did? When did? Where did and why did? What comes after that? The subject and then the base form of the verb.

dialogue.text: So let's take a look. What did you do last night? What did you do last night?
dialogue.zh: 我們來看：你昨晚做了什麼？你昨晚做了什麼？
dialogue.ja: では見てみましょう。What did you do last night? What did you do last night?
dialogue.local: So let's take a look. What did you do last night? What did you do last night?
dialogue.en: So let's take a look. What did you do last night? What did you do last night?

dialogue.text: I can answer by saying something like I watched a movie or I read a book. You'll notice that the answer is in the past simple tense.
dialogue.zh: 我可以回答說我看了電影或我讀了書。你會注意到答案是過去簡單式。
dialogue.ja: 私は映画を見たとか、本を読んだとか答えられます。答えは過去形です。
dialogue.local: I can answer by saying something like I watched a movie or I read a book. You'll notice that the answer is in the past simple tense.
dialogue.en: I can answer by saying something like I watched a movie or I read a book. You'll notice that the answer is in the past simple tense.

dialogue.text: When did you get home last night? I got home at 10 p.m.
dialogue.zh: 你昨晚幾點回家？我晚上10點回家。
dialogue.ja: 昨夜はいつ家に帰りましたか？私は午後10時に帰りました。
dialogue.local: When did you get home last night? I got home at 10 p.m.
dialogue.en: When did you get home last night? I got home at 10 p.m.

dialogue.text: Where did they eat lunch? They ate lunch at home. Again, ate is the past tense of eat. Answer in the past simple tense.
dialogue.zh: 他們在哪裡吃午餐？他們在家吃午餐。ate是eat的過去式。用過去簡單式回答。
dialogue.ja: 彼らはどこで昼食を食べましたか？彼らは家で昼食を食べました。ateはeatの過去形です。過去形で答えましょう。
dialogue.local: Where did they eat lunch? They ate lunch at home. Again, ate is the past tense of eat. Answer in the past simple tense.
dialogue.en: Where did they eat lunch? They ate lunch at home. Again, ate is the past tense of eat. Answer in the past simple tense.

dialogue.text: And finally, why did the company hire him? The company hired him because he's a hard worker.
dialogue.zh: 最後，公司為什麼雇用他？公司雇用了他，因為他很努力工作。
dialogue.ja: 最後に、なぜ会社は彼を雇ったのですか？彼は勤勉な働き手だからです。
dialogue.local: And finally, why did the company hire him? The company hired him because he's a hard worker.
dialogue.en: And finally, why did the company hire him? The company hired him because he's a hard worker.

dialogue.text: Let's move on. In this first checkup, we'll take a look at practice questions using the B verb in the past simple tense.
dialogue.zh: 我們繼續。第一個複習，我們來練習過去簡單式的B動詞問題。
dialogue.ja: 続けましょう。最初の確認テストでは、過去形のB動詞を使った練習問題を見ていきます。
dialogue.local: Let's move on. In this first checkup, we'll take a look at practice questions using the B verb in the past simple tense.
dialogue.en: Let's move on. In this first checkup, we'll take a look at practice questions using the B verb in the past simple tense.

dialogue.text: Remember, the B verbs in the past simple tense are WAS or WERE. Let's take a look at the first sentence.
dialogue.zh: 記住，過去簡單式的B動詞是WAS或WERE。看第一句。
dialogue.ja: 過去形のB動詞はWASかWEREです。最初の文を見てみましょう。
dialogue.local: Remember, the B verbs in the past simple tense are WAS or WERE. Let's take a look at the first sentence.
dialogue.en: Remember, the B verbs in the past simple tense are WAS or WERE. Let's take a look at the first sentence.

dialogue.text: He blank at work earlier. The subject here is HE. So, do we use WAS or WERE? The correct answer is WAS.
dialogue.zh: 他早些時候在工作。主詞是HE，我們用WAS還是WERE？正確答案是WAS。
dialogue.ja: He blank at work earlier. 主語はHEです。WASかWEREか？正解はWASです。
dialogue.local: He blank at work earlier. The subject here is HE. So, do we use WAS or WERE? The correct answer is WAS.
dialogue.en: He blank at work earlier. The subject here is HE. So, do we use WAS or WERE? The correct answer is WAS.

dialogue.text: He WAS at work earlier.
dialogue.zh: 他早些時候在工作。
dialogue.ja: 彼は先ほど仕事にいました。
dialogue.local: He WAS at work earlier.
dialogue.en: He WAS at work earlier.

dialogue.text: The next sentence says we blank very happy yesterday. If the subject is WE, remember the B verb is WERE.
dialogue.zh: 下一句是我們昨天很快樂。主詞是WE，B動詞是WERE。
dialogue.ja: 次の文はWe blank very happy yesterday。主語がWEならB動詞はWEREです。
dialogue.local: The next sentence says we blank very happy yesterday. If the subject is WE, remember the B verb is WERE.
dialogue.en: The next sentence says we blank very happy yesterday. If the subject is WE, remember the B verb is WERE.

dialogue.text: We were very happy yesterday.
dialogue.zh: 我們昨天很快樂。
dialogue.ja: 私たちは昨日とても幸せでした。
dialogue.local: We were very happy yesterday.
dialogue.en: We were very happy yesterday.

dialogue.text: Next, my parents or they blank worried about me. If it's they, remember, we have to say WERE.
dialogue.zh: 接著，我的父母或他們擔心我。主詞是they，B動詞是WERE。
dialogue.ja: 次に、My parents or they blank worried about me。主語がtheyならWEREを使います。
dialogue.local: Next, my parents or they blank worried about me. If it's they, remember, we have to say WERE.
dialogue.en: Next, my parents or they blank worried about me. If it's they, remember, we have to say WERE.

dialogue.text: My parents were worried about me. If I want to use the negative, I can also say my parents weren't worried about me.
dialogue.zh: 我的父母擔心我。否定句可以說my parents weren't worried about me。
dialogue.ja: 私の両親は私のことを心配していました。否定形はMy parents weren't worried about meと言えます。
dialogue.local: My parents were worried about me. If I want to use the negative, I can also say my parents weren't worried about me.
dialogue.en: My parents were worried about me. If I want to use the negative, I can also say my parents weren't worried about me.

dialogue.text: And that's possible. Now, I want you to find the mistake in the next sentence. We WASN'T good students.
dialogue.zh: 這樣說是可以的。現在，請找出下一句的錯誤：We WASN'T good students。
dialogue.ja: それも可能です。次の文の間違いを見つけてください。We WASN'T good students。
dialogue.local: And that's possible. Now, I want you to find the mistake in the next sentence. We WASN'T good students.
dialogue.en: And that's possible. Now, I want you to find the mistake in the next sentence. We WASN'T good students.

dialogue.text: We WASN'T good students. Can you figure out what's wrong? The subject here is WE. So, we don't say WASN'T. We need to say WEREN'T or the contraction weren't.
dialogue.zh: We WASN'T good students。你能找出錯誤嗎？主詞是WE，所以不能用WASN'T，要用WEREN'T或縮寫weren't。
dialogue.ja: We WASN'T good students。何が間違っているか分かりますか？主語はWEなので、WASN'Tは使いません。WEREN'Tまたは短縮形のweren'tを使います。
dialogue.local: We WASN'T good students. Can you figure out what's wrong? The subject here is WE. So, we don't say WASN'T. We need to say WEREN'T or the contraction weren't.
dialogue.en: We WASN'T good students. Can you figure out what's wrong? The subject here is WE. So, we don't say WASN'T. We need to say WEREN'T or the contraction weren't.

dialogue.text: We WEREN'T good students is the correct answer.
dialogue.zh: We WEREN'T good students才是正確答案。
dialogue.ja: 正しい答えはWe WEREN'T good studentsです。
dialogue.local: We WEREN'T good students is the correct answer.
dialogue.en: We WEREN'T good students is the correct answer.

dialogue.text: The next one says were she a teacher? Now, this is a question. So, the B verb comes at the beginning. That's correct.
dialogue.zh: 下一句是were she a teacher? 這是疑問句，B動詞放在句首，這是對的。
dialogue.ja: 次はWere she a teacher? これは疑問文で、B動詞が文頭に来るのは正しいです。
dialogue.local: The next one says were she a teacher? Now, this is a question. So, the B verb comes at the beginning. That's correct.
dialogue.en: The next one says were she a teacher? Now, this is a question. So, the B verb comes at the beginning. That's correct.

dialogue.text: But the subject here is SHE. Therefore, we need to start with WAS. Was she a teacher?
dialogue.zh: 但主詞是SHE，所以要用WAS開頭。Was she a teacher?
dialogue.ja: しかし、主語はSHEなので、WASで始める必要があります。Was she a teacher?
dialogue.local: But the subject here is SHE. Therefore, we need to start with WAS. Was she a teacher?
dialogue.en: But the subject here is SHE. Therefore, we need to start with WAS. Was she a teacher?

dialogue.text: And finally, they WASN'T at school. The subject is THEY. So, the answer is THEY WEREN'T at school.
dialogue.zh: 最後，they WASN'T at school。主詞是THEY，正確答案是THEY WEREN'T at school。
dialogue.ja: 最後に、They WASN'T at school。主語はTHEYなので、正しくはThey WEREN'T at schoolです。
dialogue.local: And finally, they WASN'T at school. The subject is THEY. So, the answer is THEY WEREN'T at school.
dialogue.en: And finally, they WASN'T at school. The subject is THEY. So, the answer is THEY WEREN'T at school.

dialogue.text: You can use the contraction weren't, or were not. Let's move on to the next check-up.
dialogue.zh: 你可以用縮寫weren't或were not。我們繼續下一個複習。
dialogue.ja: 短縮形のweren'tやwere notを使えます。次の確認テストに進みましょう。
dialogue.local: You can use the contraction weren't, or were not. Let's move on to the next check-up.
dialogue.en: You can use the contraction weren't, or were not. Let's move on to the next check-up.

dialogue.text: Now, let's practice regular verbs in the past simple tense. Take a look at the first sentence. He blank at home. The verb is study.
dialogue.zh: 現在，我們練習過去簡單式的規則動詞。看第一句：He blank at home。動詞是study。
dialogue.ja: 次に、過去形の規則動詞を練習しましょう。最初の文はHe blank at home。動詞はstudyです。
dialogue.local: Now, let's practice regular verbs in the past simple tense. Take a look at the first sentence. He blank at home. The verb is study.
dialogue.en: Now, let's practice regular verbs in the past simple tense. Take a look at the first sentence. He blank at home. The verb is study.

dialogue.text: Remember, when changing a regular verb into the past tense, we add D or ED to the end of the verb.
dialogue.zh: 記住，規則動詞變成過去式時，我們在動詞後加D或ED。
dialogue.ja: 規則動詞を過去形にする時は、動詞の後ろにDかEDを付けます。
dialogue.local: Remember, when changing a regular verb into the past tense, we add D or ED to the end of the verb.
dialogue.en: Remember, when changing a regular verb into the past tense, we add D or ED to the end of the verb.

dialogue.text: However, there's a separate rule for words that end in Y, such as study. We drop the Y and we add IED.
dialogue.zh: 不過，像study這類以Y結尾的字，有特別規則。我們把Y改成IED。
dialogue.ja: ただし、studyのようにYで終わる単語は別のルールがあります。Yを落としてIEDを付けます。
dialogue.local: However, there's a separate rule for words that end in Y, such as study. We drop the Y and we add IED.
dialogue.en: However, there's a separate rule for words that end in Y, such as study. We drop the Y and we add IED.

dialogue.text: So, the correct answer is He studied at home.
dialogue.zh: 所以正確答案是He studied at home。
dialogue.ja: だから、正しい答えはHe studied at homeです。
dialogue.local: So, the correct answer is He studied at home.
dialogue.en: So, the correct answer is He studied at home.

dialogue.text: The next sentence says we did not use pencils. Remember, for the negative, we always use did not, no matter what the subject.
dialogue.zh: 下一句是we did not use pencils。記住，否定句不管主詞是誰，都用did not。
dialogue.ja: 次の文はWe did not use pencilsです。否定文は主語に関係なくdid notを使います。
dialogue.local: The next sentence says we did not use pencils. Remember, for the negative, we always use did not, no matter what the subject.
dialogue.en: The next sentence says we did not use pencils. Remember, for the negative, we always use did not, no matter what the subject.

dialogue.text: You can also use the contraction didn't. Now, what do we do to the verb? We keep it as is. We do not change it.
dialogue.zh: 你也可以用縮寫didn't。動詞保持原形，不變化。
dialogue.ja: 短縮形のdidn'tも使えます。動詞は原形のままです。変えません。
dialogue.local: You can also use the contraction didn't. Now, what do we do to the verb? We keep it as is. We do not change it.
dialogue.en: You can also use the contraction didn't. Now, what do we do to the verb? We keep it as is. We do not change it.

dialogue.text: We didn't, or we did not use pencils.
dialogue.zh: We didn't use pencils 或 We did not use pencils。
dialogue.ja: We didn't use pencils または We did not use pencils。
dialogue.local: We didn't, or we did not use pencils.
dialogue.en: We didn't, or we did not use pencils.

dialogue.text: The next sentence says his friends, or they, walked to the gym. What's the past tense of walk? We simply have to add ED because it's a regular verb.
dialogue.zh: 下一句是his friends或they walked to the gym。walk的過去式是walked，因為是規則動詞，我們加ED。
dialogue.ja: 次の文はHis friendsまたはThey walked to the gymです。walkの過去形はwalkedで、規則動詞なのでEDを付けます。
dialogue.local: The next sentence says his friends, or they, walked to the gym. What's the past tense of walk? We simply have to add ED because it's a regular verb.
dialogue.en: The next sentence says his friends, or they, walked to the gym. What's the past tense of walk? We simply have to add ED because it's a regular verb.

dialogue.text: His friends walked to the gym.
dialogue.zh: 他的朋友們走路去健身房。
dialogue.ja: 彼の友達はジムまで歩きました。
dialogue.local: His friends walked to the gym.
dialogue.en: His friends walked to the gym.

dialogue.text: Now, find the mistake in the next sentence. She didn't like math. Didn't is correct. However, remember, we keep the verb as is in the base form.
dialogue.zh: 現在找下一句錯誤：She didn't like math。didn't是對的，但動詞要保持原形。
dialogue.ja: 次の文の間違いを見つけてください。She didn't like math。didn'tは正しいですが、動詞は原形のままです。
dialogue.local: Now, find the mistake in the next sentence. She didn't like math. Didn't is correct. However, remember, we keep the verb as is in the base form.
dialogue.en: Now, find the mistake in the next sentence. She didn't like math. Didn't is correct. However, remember, we keep the verb as is in the base form.

dialogue.text: So, we don't say liked, we say like. She didn't like math.
dialogue.zh: 所以不是liked，是like。She didn't like math。
dialogue.ja: だからlikedではなくlikeを使います。She didn't like math。
dialogue.local: So, we don't say liked, we say like. She didn't like math.
dialogue.en: So, we don't say liked, we say like. She didn't like math.

dialogue.text: The next sentence says, did it rain this morning? Now, this is a question. In a question, it's right to start the sentence with DID.
dialogue.zh: 下一句是Did it rain this morning? 這是疑問句，開頭用DID是對的。
dialogue.ja: 次の文はDid it rain this morning? これは疑問文で、DIDで始めるのは正しいです。
dialogue.local: The next sentence says, did it rain this morning? Now, this is a question. In a question, it's right to start the sentence with DID.
dialogue.en: The next sentence says, did it rain this morning? Now, this is a question. In a question, it's right to start the sentence with DID.

dialogue.text: Did it rain? Do you notice the mistake? Remember, we do not use the past tense form in the question. We use the base form of the verb.
dialogue.zh: Did it rain? 你注意到錯誤了嗎？疑問句中動詞不用過去式，要用原形。
dialogue.ja: Did it rain? 間違いに気づきましたか？疑問文では動詞の過去形は使わず、原形を使います。
dialogue.local: Did it rain? Do you notice the mistake? Remember, we do not use the past tense form in the question. We use the base form of the verb.
dialogue.en: Did it rain? Do you notice the mistake? Remember, we do not use the past tense form in the question. We use the base form of the verb.

dialogue.text: Did it rain this morning?
dialogue.zh: Did it rain this morning?
dialogue.ja: 最後に、they not play the piano です。動詞は動作動詞なので、not の前に DID が必要です。
dialogue.local: Did it rain this morning?
dialogue.en: Did it rain this morning?

dialogue.text: And finally, they did not play the piano. The verb is an action verb, so we need a DID in front of the not.
dialogue.zh: 最後，他們沒有彈鋼琴。動詞是動作動詞，所以not前面要加DID。
dialogue.ja: 最後に、They did not play the piano。動詞は動作動詞なので、notの前にDIDを置きます。
dialogue.local: And finally, they did not play the piano. The verb is an action verb, so we need a DID in front of the not.
dialogue.en: And finally, they did not play the piano. The verb is an action verb, so we need a DID in front of the not.

dialogue.text: They did not play the piano.
dialogue.zh: They did not play the piano。
dialogue.ja: They did not play the piano。
dialogue.local: They did not play the piano.
dialogue.en: They did not play the piano.

dialogue.text: Let's move on to the next checkup. Now, I'll talk about irregular verbs in the past simple tense.
dialogue.zh: 我們繼續下一個複習。現在，我要談談過去簡單式的不規則動詞。
dialogue.ja: 次の確認テストに進みましょう。今度は過去形の不規則動詞について話します。
dialogue.local: Let's move on to the next checkup. Now, I'll talk about irregular verbs in the past simple tense.
dialogue.en: Let's move on to the next checkup. Now, I'll talk about irregular verbs in the past simple tense.

dialogue.text: Take a look at the first sentence. He blank to school, and the verb is run. Run is an irregular verb, so the past tense form is ran.
dialogue.zh: 看第一句：He blank to school。動詞是run，run是不規則動詞，過去式是ran。
dialogue.ja: 最初の文を見てください。He blank to school。動詞はrunで、不規則動詞なので過去形はranです。
dialogue.local: Take a look at the first sentence. He blank to school, and the verb is run. Run is an irregular verb, so the past tense form is ran.
dialogue.en: Take a look at the first sentence. He blank to school, and the verb is run. Run is an irregular verb, so the past tense form is ran.

dialogue.text: He ran to school.
dialogue.zh: 他跑去學校。
dialogue.ja: 彼は学校へ走って行きました。
dialogue.local: He ran to school.
dialogue.en: He ran to school.

dialogue.text: The next sentence says, we did not grow flowers. Remember, no matter what the subject in the negative form, we say did not or didn't. Then, we keep the verb in its base form.
dialogue.zh: 下一句是we did not grow flowers。記住，否定句不管主詞是誰，都用did not或didn't，動詞保持原形。
dialogue.ja: 次の文はWe did not grow flowersです。否定文は主語に関係なくdid notまたはdidn'tを使い、動詞は原形のままです。
dialogue.local: The next sentence says, we did not grow flowers. Remember, no matter what the subject in the negative form, we say did not or didn't. Then, we keep the verb in its base form.
dialogue.en: The next sentence says, we did not grow flowers. Remember, no matter what the subject in the negative form, we say did not or didn't. Then, we keep the verb in its base form.

dialogue.text: We did not grow, or we didn't grow flowers.
dialogue.zh: We did not grow flowers 或 We didn't grow flowers。
dialogue.ja: We did not grow flowers または We didn't grow flowers。
dialogue.local: We did not grow, or we didn't grow flowers.
dialogue.en: We did not grow, or we didn't grow flowers.

dialogue.text: The next sentence says, where did you teach last year? This is a question. Again, all we need to put is DID.
dialogue.zh: 下一句是where did you teach last year? 這是疑問句，我們只要加DID。
dialogue.ja: 次の文はWhere did you teach last year? これは疑問文で、DIDを使います。
dialogue.local: The next sentence says, where did you teach last year? This is a question. Again, all we need to put is DID.
dialogue.en: The next sentence says, where did you teach last year? This is a question. Again, all we need to put is DID.

dialogue.text: Where did you teach last year? It doesn't matter what the subject is. We always go with DID.
dialogue.zh: Where did you teach last year? 不管主詞是誰，都用DID。
dialogue.ja: Where did you teach last year? 主語に関係なくDIDを使います。
dialogue.local: Where did you teach last year? It doesn't matter what the subject is. We always go with DID.
dialogue.en: Where did you teach last year? It doesn't matter what the subject is. We always go with DID.

dialogue.text: Next, try to find the mistake in the next sentence. He didn't sold newspapers.
dialogue.zh: 接著找出下一句錯誤：He didn't sold newspapers。
dialogue.ja: 次の文の間違いを見つけてください。He didn't sold newspapers。
dialogue.local: Next, try to find the mistake in the next sentence. He didn't sold newspapers.
dialogue.en: Next, try to find the mistake in the next sentence. He didn't sold newspapers.

dialogue.text: Remember, in the negative, didn't is correct for whatever subject there is. However, we need to keep the verb in its base form.
dialogue.zh: 記住，否定句用didn't是對的，但動詞要用原形。
dialogue.ja: 否定文ではdidn'tは正しいですが、動詞は原形を使います。
dialogue.local: Remember, in the negative, didn't is correct for whatever subject there is. However, we need to keep the verb in its base form.
dialogue.en: Remember, in the negative, didn't is correct for whatever subject there is. However, we need to keep the verb in its base form.

dialogue.text: So, the correct answer is, he didn't sell newspapers.
dialogue.zh: 正確答案是he didn't sell newspapers。
dialogue.ja: 正しい答えはHe didn't sell newspapersです。
dialogue.local: So, the correct answer is, he didn't sell newspapers.
dialogue.en: So, the correct answer is, he didn't sell newspapers.

dialogue.text: The next sentence says, did she sing a song? You'll notice it's a similar problem here.
dialogue.zh: 下一句是did she sing a song? 這裡有類似的問題。
dialogue.ja: 次の文はDid she sing a song? ここでも似た問題があります。
dialogue.local: The next sentence says, did she sing a song? You'll notice it's a similar problem here.
dialogue.en: The next sentence says, did she sing a song? You'll notice it's a similar problem here.

dialogue.text: Singing is the irregular past tense form of sing. But in a question, if it starts with DID, we use the base form.
dialogue.zh: Singing是sing的不規則過去式，但疑問句用DID開頭時，要用原形。
dialogue.ja: Singingはsingの不規則過去形ですが、疑問文でDIDがある場合は原形を使います。
dialogue.local: Singing is the irregular past tense form of sing. But in a question, if it starts with DID, we use the base form.
dialogue.en: Singing is the irregular past tense form of sing. But in a question, if it starts with DID, we use the base form.

dialogue.text: Did she sing a song?
dialogue.zh: Did she sing a song?
dialogue.ja: Did she sing a song?
dialogue.local: Did she sing a song?
dialogue.en: Did she sing a song?

dialogue.text: And finally, we took it home. Does that sound right? Took is the past tense of take.
dialogue.zh: 最後，我們帶回家。這樣說對嗎？took是take的過去式。
dialogue.ja: 最後に、We took it home。正しいですか？tookはtakeの過去形です。
dialogue.local: And finally, we took it home. Does that sound right? Took is the past tense of take.
dialogue.en: And finally, we took it home. Does that sound right? Took is the past tense of take.

dialogue.text: Great job, everyone. Let's move on.
dialogue.zh: 大家做得很好，我們繼續。
dialogue.ja: みなさん、よくできました。続けましょう。
dialogue.local: Great job, everyone. Let's move on.
dialogue.en: Great job, everyone. Let's move on.

dialogue.text: Wow, we learned a lot in this video. Keep studying and reviewing the past simple tense. It's an essential tense that will help you talk about the past.
dialogue.zh: 哇，我們在這個影片學了很多。繼續學習和複習過去簡單式。這是很重要的時態，能幫助你談論過去。
dialogue.ja: この動画でたくさん学びましたね。過去形の勉強と復習を続けてください。過去について話すのに欠かせない時制です。
dialogue.local: Wow, we learned a lot in this video. Keep studying and reviewing the past simple tense. It's an essential tense that will help you talk about the past.
dialogue.en: Wow, we learned a lot in this video. Keep studying and reviewing the past simple tense. It's an essential tense that will help you talk about the past.

dialogue.text: Keep studying English and I'll see you in the next video. Bye!
dialogue.zh: 繼續學習英文，我們下個影片見。再見！
dialogue.ja: 英語の勉強を続けて、次の動画でお会いしましょう。さようなら！
dialogue.local: Keep studying English and I'll see you in the next video. Bye!
dialogue.en: Keep studying English and I'll see you in the next video. Bye!
